tasks.title: The embeddings warm-up thread loads torch and faiss, holding the Windows loader lock for that import's length
tasks.verify: A tool that starts a thread returns within its bound while the embeddings warm-up is in flight, measured with USE_SEMANTIC_SEARCH=1 so the warm-up actually runs. THE SAME MECHANISM AS THE NLTK ONE, ONE DEGREE MILDER, and the difference is the whole question. Uncommitted in the working tree, server.py now reads stdin through a polling reader that never parks a read on the pipe, which removed the unbounded part: an import in a background thread no longer advances one DLL per client message. But a native-extension load still holds the Windows loader lock for its own duration, and torch plus faiss are not a short import - so Thread.start() anywhere else in the process still waits that long. FIRST ESTABLISH WHETHER THIS IS WORTH FIXING AT ALL, with a number: measure how long a concurrent Thread.start() actually blocks during the warm-up. If it is a second or two, say so and record the task as not worth the complexity rather than building a fix nobody needs - a measurement that closes a task is a good outcome here. WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY MEASURED: the liveness sweep in test_mcp_tool_dispatch.py runs with USE_SEMANTIC_SEARCH=0, so the warm-up never starts there and the existing zero-timeout result says nothing about this path. Any measurement must turn it on. THE PRIOR ART IS IN THE TREE AND SHOULD BE READ BEFORE DESIGNING: features.py's nltk warm-up and kb/search/_retrieval.py's embeddings warm-up already share a deadline-on-a-named-thread shape, and server.py's polling reader carries a comment explaining the pipe mechanism. Both are granted r:. kb/search/__init__.py asserts each sub-mixin's exact method set, so a new helper in _retrieval.py must be a module-level function rather than a method - a previous task hit this and it is not in your grant to change. TEST PAIRING, checked on the filesystem: there is no test_retrieval.py and no kb/search/test_*.py at this head; test_mcp_startup.py owns the startup and warm-up assertions (it already asserts 'Embeddings warm-up deadline missed' reaches stderr) and is the home. SABOTAGE, if a fix is built: revert it and confirm the new assertion FAILS on its own deadline rather than hanging, printing the changed region from disk FIRST. If the measurement says no fix is warranted, no sabotage is required - say that explicitly instead. Scope the footprint check with `git diff --name-only -- kb/search/_retrieval.py test_mcp_startup.py`.

ESTABLISHED BY A PRIOR TASK READING THE SOURCE, and cheap to re-confirm rather than take on trust: call_tool in server.py is a single blocking request-to-response with no progressToken threaded anywhere, and the installed mcp package (mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py, mcp/shared/session.py) was inspected and found to carry no plumbing this server uses. The consequence is concrete: check_updates with auto_update=true can re-index hundreds of documents and the caller sees nothing until it returns, which is what made issue #17's reporter abort a working run at 30 minutes. add_documents_bulk has the same shape - its handler never passes the progress_callback its kb method accepts. THE MCP SPEC HAS notifications/progress AND progressToken; whether THIS SDK version exposes them to a lowlevel Server is the actual open question. Check the installed package version and its own source before designing, and if the answer is that it cannot, that is a legitimate close - record the version and the file you read. IF IT CAN: the two handlers that would use it are granted r: as the callers to keep consistent with, not as files to edit in this task - wire the transport-level capability in server.py and say which handler should adopt it next. Do not rewrite both handlers here. DO NOT DEGRADE WHAT ALREADY WORKS: the per-document logger heartbeat added to check_all_updates is the operator-visible channel and must keep working whatever happens to the client-visible one. TEST PAIRING, checked on the filesystem: there is no live test_server.py (archive/tests/test_server.py is archived and not collected), so test_mcp_startup.py is the home for any assertion, and it already drives real stdio sessions through MCPSession. SABOTAGE, if a capability is wired: revert it and confirm the new assertion FAILS rather than silently passing on a client that never receives a notification, printing the changed region from disk FIRST. Scope the footprint check with `git diff --name-only -- server.py test_mcp_startup.py`.

closed.title: Every tool that reaches _preprocess_text hangs forever in a long-lived stdio server
closed.reason: ROOT CAUSE IS WINDOWS I/O SERIALISATION ON THE STDIN FILE OBJECT, and both candidates this plan named were refuted by bisect rather than argument. The BLAS-linked DLL initialisations inside nltk's import chain touch stdin; the MCP stdio transport always has a read pending there, so the import waits for a client message while the client waits for the reply. Not a deadlock - an unbounded wait on client traffic. I reproduced the mechanism with my own harness: no reader 0.229s, an IDLE extra thread 0.235s (the control that rules out generic thread interference), a pending os.read(0,1) HUNG past 25s, and the same shape released 0.2s after one byte was written to the pipe. It explains every earlier observation, including why the HTTP transport returned the identical query in 724ms and why my own isolation tests all looked clean - none of them had a pending stdin read. Fixed by moving the import to a named daemon thread behind an env-tunable deadline with both ends logged; 34 passed, re-run independently.
